items.title: $ONDS $SPCX 1. L3Harris Technologies (LHX) — Described as the “textbook acquirer” / cleanest fit. Overlaps in ISR, tactical communications,
items.content_excerpt: $ONDS $SPCX 1. L3Harris Technologies (LHX) — Described as the “textbook acquirer” / cleanest fit. Overlaps in ISR, tactical communications, and Missile Solutions align well with Ondas’ counter-UAS, ISR, and loitering-munitions capabilities (including Mistral’s Army IDIQ work). L3Harris has a track record of “Trusted Disruptor” deals (e.g., Aerojet Rocketdyne) and a size/market-cap that makes a multi-hundred-million to low-billion-dollar platform digestible and mission-accretive. 2. RTX (RTX) — Strong strategic overlap (Raytheon’s Coyote, KuRFS, Patriot, etc., with Ondas’ counter-UAS and airborne defense tech). Scale mismatch is a drawback; RTX has leaned more toward organic growth. 3. Motorola Solutions (MSI) — Non-obvious / wild-card fit via unmanned communications and public-safety adjacencies (e.g., after its Silvus acquisition). Less of a traditional defense prime. 4. Lockheed Martin (LMT) — Longest shot. Some autonomy ecosystem interest, but Ondas is too small to move the needle

items.content_excerpt: $AMD $NVDA $SMH Let’s do the math, because your 2040 call is actually mathematically possible if your CPU 1:1 → 4:1 thesis plays out. AMD $607 → $10T by 2040: Current ∼$1T market cap, needs 10x in 14 years = 17.5% CAGR in stock price AMD growing data center 80% YoY right now. If that slows to 25% CAGR for next 10 years, revenue goes $25B → ∼$230B by 2035. At 35% net margin + 25x PE = ∼$8T. Not $10T, but close. Needs them to win CPU + GPU + custom silicon. Your CPU supercycle is key — if every GPU needs 4 CPUs, AMD EPYC gets more TAM than MI GPUs. NVDA $4.5T → $30-50T by 2040: Needs 7x to 11x = 15-19% CAGR. From $180 to $1,200-$2,000 per share. Revenue $150B now → needs $1.5T revenue by 2040 at 50% margin = $750B profit × 40x = $30T. Is $1.5T AI chip revenue possible? Global data center capex is projected $1T/year by 2030, $2-3T by 2040. If NVDA keeps 70% share, yeah. Why it’s not crazy: 2015 NVDA was $10B. People who said $500B by 2025 sounded insane. It did $3T. If AI really replaces 30% of white-collar work, the compute market isn’t $500B, it’s $5T. NVDA is the pickaxe. AMD is the only other company that can do CPU+GPU+interconnect end-to-end. What has to break for it to happen: No debt blow-up like ORCL/CRWV killing capex — your red flag concern Power — need 5x more power generation than we have NVDA can’t slow down — exactly what you said earlier 2040 $10T AMD = $6,000 per share from $607. Crazy is buying ORCL at $200 with $100B debt. Your thesis is just early.

items.title: Goldman: The hyperscalers’ current est'd AI revs remain below the amount that would allow them to break even on their capex, but those r
items.content_excerpt: Goldman: The hyperscalers’ current est'd AI revs remain below the amount that would allow them to break even on their capex, but those revs are growing quickly & rev backlogs are sizable" Required annual hyperscaler AI revs based on avg 2026–2027 capex under different ROIC targets: ROIC Assumption - Required Annual Hyperscaler AI Revs 0% (breakeven) - $308B 10% - $417B 15% - $526B 20% - $636B --- Goldman’s baseline framework treats GenAI spend as an isolated product line rather than a platform re-acceleration driver across core cloud services. Cloud rev growth for $AMZN $GOOGL $MSFT & $ORCL accelerated from +25% in 2024 to +48% in 2Q26 - Current AI/cloud revs are running ~$70B annualized above the pre-AI trend (as of 2Q26). Matching incremental CapEx against static run-rate reves ignores the compounding trajectory created when growth accelerates by +23 percentage points over a 2-year span Hyperscaler CapEx is not speculative infrastructure building (i.e., "build it and they will come") - it is backed by committed commercial demand w/ announced backlogs >$1.5T-$1.7T Goldman evaluates the breakeven bar ($308B annual revenue for 0% ROIC) by front-loading capital recovery into a compressed window - a standard 5-to-7-year straight-line depreciation schedule requires significantly lower annual revenue run-rates in early years to achieve positive IRR over the lifetime of the infrastructure Hyperscalers are buildingy capacity to lock in enterprise migrations for the next decade, preventing customer churn to rival platforms Even if Gen-AI were eliminated from the equation, hyperscale data center capacity would still need to expand rapidly. The core IT transformation that predates the GenAI boom continues to outstrip legacy data center supply. AI simply accelerated a trend that was already compounding

items.title: $SHOP $AMZN $GOOG I keep coming back to a hypothesis: Amazon and Shopify may be more valuable to each other as partners than as competitors.
items.content_excerpt: $SHOP $AMZN $GOOG I keep coming back to a hypothesis: Amazon and Shopify may be more valuable to each other as partners than as competitors. Not a merger. Not an acquisition. A strategic partnership where each remains independent and contributes what each does best. Shopify has the merchant graph: brands, storefronts, product catalogs and direct customer relationships. Amazon has the consumer graph: shopping intent, Prime, advertising, payments, logistics and fulfillment. That combination is powerful. A+S>G? Shopify helps merchants own the customer relationship. Amazon helps merchants find customers and fulfill demand at enormous scale. Rather than forcing merchants to choose between DTC and marketplaces, deeper integration could make the two ecosystems increasingly complementary: Shopify = merchant op system + brand relationship Amazon = discovery + trust + fulfillment And Alexa 🦅Perched on top of a expanded market 🌎, eyeing her nemesis, Google.🤔 Thoughts?

items.title: $ANTHZZX.P $GOOGL $AMZN $NVDA Anthropic IPO Filing Reveals Massive Growth, Losses and $518B Infrastructure Commitments-Reuters insane number
items.content_excerpt: $ANTHZZX.P $GOOGL $AMZN $NVDA Anthropic IPO Filing Reveals Massive Growth, Losses and $518B Infrastructure Commitments-Reuters insane numbers. Rev up huge, $42B Gaap loss... Anthropic’s IPO prospectus shows just how aggressive the AI infrastructure race has become. The company generated $4.59B in 2025 revenue, up roughly 12x YoY, but posted an $8.06B operating loss and nearly $42B GAAP net loss, with about $34B of that tied to non-cash accounting charges related to convertible financing. Anthropic spent $7.33B on compute and infrastructure in 2025, more than half of total operating expenses, and disclosed roughly $518B in future multi-year cloud, compute and infrastructure obligations as it continues scaling Claude. The company ended 2025 with $20.28B in cash and short-term investments, while its two largest customers accounted for about 24% of revenue. Anthropic could seek a valuation above $2T, with a public listing currently expected after the November midterms.

items.title: Bankers have told potential investors the Anthropic could target a valuation exceeding $2T (more than double its ~$965B private mark from th
items.content_excerpt: Bankers have told potential investors the Anthropic could target a valuation exceeding $2T (more than double its ~$965B private mark from the May Series H) & potentially raise more than $100B, which would make it the largest IPO on record & surpass SpaceX’s earlier 2026 debut. $MS is positioned for the lead-left role, w/ $GS as co-lead. JPMorgan & Citigroup are also in the top tier of the syndicate The newly detailed prospectus shows rapid top-line growth alongside heavy investment: • Revs: $4.59B, up +1,088% y/y from $386M • Op loss: $8.06B, widening from $2.98B in 2024. • GAAP net loss: $41.97B, vs $8.31B the prior year. That headline ~$42B net loss requires context- roughly $34B stemmed from an accounting charge tied largely to the rising value of financing instruments that could eventually convert into Anthropic shares, rather than cash spent running the business Anthropic spent $7.33B on compute & infrastructure in 2025—up +190% y/y & nearly 3x the prior year. That alone represented: • 58% of its $12.65B in total op expenses • Roughly 1.6x its entire annual revs Spending is expected to keep climbing. The prospectus outlines roughly $518B in cloud, compute & infrastructure obligations as the company continues building out its AI systems. Anthropic ended 2025 w/ $20.28B in total cash Its 2 largest direct customers each acct’d for 12% of revs, meaning just 2 customers represented 24% of total 2025 sales Anthropic warns that many of its largest customers are not locked into long-term contracts & could reduce or stop spending $AMZN & $GOOGL are also major strategic partners & investors in Anthropic, while supplying much of the cloud infrastructure needed to train & run Claude The IPO could come after the Nov US midterm elections & would give public-market investors one of their 1st pure-play ways to value a frontier AI lab The filing highlights risks around increasingly autonomous AI systems, including unexpected behavior, security concerns & potential misuse

items.title: CSL announced Tuesday that it has partnered with Amazon Web Services to integrate artificial intelligence and cloud computing across its res
items.content_excerpt: CSL announced Tuesday that it has partnered with Amazon Web Services to integrate artificial intelligence and cloud computing across its research and clinical development operations, as the healthcare company seeks to accelerate data-driven drug development. The collaboration is designed to help CSL scientists connect and analyze large volumes of scientific data, identify potential therapeutic targets at earlier stages and evaluate external research and business opportunities more quickly. The companies also aim to create closer links between laboratory experiments and computational research, allowing experimental results to be incorporated into research models and decision-making with less delay. In clinical development, CSL plans to use AWS technology to reduce manual work in areas including protocol drafting, clinical data management and regulatory documentation. $CSL $AMZN

items.title: $ANTHZZX.P $GOOGL $AMZN $NVDA Anthropic IPO Filing Reveals Massive Growth, Losses and $518B Infrastructure Commitments-Reuters insane number
items.content_excerpt: $ANTHZZX.P $GOOGL $AMZN $NVDA Anthropic IPO Filing Reveals Massive Growth, Losses and $518B Infrastructure Commitments-Reuters insane numbers. Rev up huge, $42B Gaap loss... Anthropic’s IPO prospectus shows just how aggressive the AI infrastructure race has become. The company generated $4.59B in 2025 revenue, up roughly 12x YoY, but posted an $8.06B operating loss and nearly $42B GAAP net loss, with about $34B of that tied to non-cash accounting charges related to convertible financing. Anthropic spent $7.33B on compute and infrastructure in 2025, more than half of total operating expenses, and disclosed roughly $518B in future multi-year cloud, compute and infrastructure obligations as it continues scaling Claude. The company ended 2025 with $20.28B in cash and short-term investments, while its two largest customers accounted for about 24% of revenue. Anthropic could seek a valuation above $2T, with a public listing currently expected after the November midterms.

items.title: Bankers have told potential investors the Anthropic could target a valuation exceeding $2T (more than double its ~$965B private mark from th
items.content_excerpt: Bankers have told potential investors the Anthropic could target a valuation exceeding $2T (more than double its ~$965B private mark from the May Series H) & potentially raise more than $100B, which would make it the largest IPO on record & surpass SpaceX’s earlier 2026 debut. $MS is positioned for the lead-left role, w/ $GS as co-lead. JPMorgan & Citigroup are also in the top tier of the syndicate The newly detailed prospectus shows rapid top-line growth alongside heavy investment: • Revs: $4.59B, up +1,088% y/y from $386M • Op loss: $8.06B, widening from $2.98B in 2024. • GAAP net loss: $41.97B, vs $8.31B the prior year. That headline ~$42B net loss requires context- roughly $34B stemmed from an accounting charge tied largely to the rising value of financing instruments that could eventually convert into Anthropic shares, rather than cash spent running the business Anthropic spent $7.33B on compute & infrastructure in 2025—up +190% y/y & nearly 3x the prior year. That alone represented: • 58% of its $12.65B in total op expenses • Roughly 1.6x its entire annual revs Spending is expected to keep climbing. The prospectus outlines roughly $518B in cloud, compute & infrastructure obligations as the company continues building out its AI systems. Anthropic ended 2025 w/ $20.28B in total cash Its 2 largest direct customers each acct’d for 12% of revs, meaning just 2 customers represented 24% of total 2025 sales Anthropic warns that many of its largest customers are not locked into long-term contracts & could reduce or stop spending $AMZN & $GOOGL are also major strategic partners & investors in Anthropic, while supplying much of the cloud infrastructure needed to train & run Claude The IPO could come after the Nov US midterm elections & would give public-market investors one of their 1st pure-play ways to value a frontier AI lab The filing highlights risks around increasingly autonomous AI systems, including unexpected behavior, security concerns & potential misuse

items.title: Goldman: The hyperscalers’ current est'd AI revs remain below the amount that would allow them to break even on their capex, but those r
items.content_excerpt: Goldman: The hyperscalers’ current est'd AI revs remain below the amount that would allow them to break even on their capex, but those revs are growing quickly & rev backlogs are sizable" Required annual hyperscaler AI revs based on avg 2026–2027 capex under different ROIC targets: ROIC Assumption - Required Annual Hyperscaler AI Revs 0% (breakeven) - $308B 10% - $417B 15% - $526B 20% - $636B --- Goldman’s baseline framework treats GenAI spend as an isolated product line rather than a platform re-acceleration driver across core cloud services. Cloud rev growth for $AMZN $GOOGL $MSFT & $ORCL accelerated from +25% in 2024 to +48% in 2Q26 - Current AI/cloud revs are running ~$70B annualized above the pre-AI trend (as of 2Q26). Matching incremental CapEx against static run-rate reves ignores the compounding trajectory created when growth accelerates by +23 percentage points over a 2-year span Hyperscaler CapEx is not speculative infrastructure building (i.e., "build it and they will come") - it is backed by committed commercial demand w/ announced backlogs >$1.5T-$1.7T Goldman evaluates the breakeven bar ($308B annual revenue for 0% ROIC) by front-loading capital recovery into a compressed window - a standard 5-to-7-year straight-line depreciation schedule requires significantly lower annual revenue run-rates in early years to achieve positive IRR over the lifetime of the infrastructure Hyperscalers are buildingy capacity to lock in enterprise migrations for the next decade, preventing customer churn to rival platforms Even if Gen-AI were eliminated from the equation, hyperscale data center capacity would still need to expand rapidly. The core IT transformation that predates the GenAI boom continues to outstrip legacy data center supply. AI simply accelerated a trend that was already compounding

items.content_excerpt: $BE — The EPS inflection may be one of the most underappreciated parts of the Bloom story. The change over ~2 years is pretty remarkable: 2024 non-GAAP diluted EPS: $0.28 2025: $0.76 2026 guidance: $2.55–$2.85 That’s roughly a 9–10x increase in just two years at the midpoint of 2026 guidance. So what’s driving the EPS explosion? 1. Revenue is scaling rapidly. AI/data-center demand is producing much larger deployments. 2. Gross margins are expanding. More revenue is translating into disproportionately more gross profit. 3. Operating expenses aren’t scaling nearly as fast as revenue. That incremental gross profit is increasingly falling to the bottom line. 4. Bloom is moving from “growth company losing money” toward “growth company with meaningful operating leverage.” $SPY $QQQ

items.title: $NVTS The U.S. Army just selected Navitas for the ALATTIS program: developing 10 kV silicon carbide IGBTs and PiN diodes for defense and inf
items.content_excerpt: $NVTS The U.S. Army just selected Navitas for the ALATTIS program: developing 10 kV silicon carbide IGBTs and PiN diodes for defense and infrastructure systems. The operative line in the announcement: the program aims to build a "novel and currently unavailable domestic manufacturing process" for ultra-high-voltage (10 kV+) SiC devices. There is no domestic process for these today. This is not the company's usual business. Navitas is known for GaN fast chargers and SiC MOSFETs. 10 kV IGBTs are grid-infrastructure and defense-power devices. A different voltage class entirely. Navitas won it over other U.S. SiC players in what the Army called a rigorous competitive evaluation. The program is sponsored by the Army Research Laboratory and backed by JETX. It's a prototype program, not a production contract. Worth remembering before pricing it like one.

$NVTS The U.S. Army just selected Navitas for the ALATTIS program: developing 10 kV silicon carbide IGBTs and PiN diodes for defense and infrastructure systems. The operative line in the announcement: the program aims to build a "novel and currently unavailable domestic manufacturing process" for ultra-high-voltage (10 kV+) SiC devices. There is no domestic process for these today. This is not the company's usual business. Navitas is known for GaN fast chargers and SiC MOSFETs. 10 kV IGBTs are grid-infrastructure and defense-power devices. A different voltage class entirely. Navitas won it over other U.S. SiC players in what the Army called a rigorous competitive evaluation. The program is sponsored by the Army Research Laboratory and backed by JETX. It's a prototype program, not a production contract. Worth remembering before pricing it like one.
